source.title: Most Stones Removed with Same Row or Column

teaching.hint: How much can a chain of shared-row or shared-column relationships allow you to remove, even when its endpoints do not directly share a coordinate?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Connected groups cannot lose their last stone, but a spanning-tree removal order lets every other stone go. Coordinate labels recover these groups without enumerating every pair.
solution_outline.approach: Treat each used row and each used column as separate labels. For every stone, join its row label to its column label in a disjoint-set structure. Count the resulting components among used labels and subtract that count from the number of stones.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The disjoint-set partition represents connectivity through processed stones. Row and column labels occupy separate namespaces; labels are created only when a stone uses them.
solution_outline.correctness: In the stone graph, no component can lose its last stone because no stone outside it shares a row or column. Root a spanning tree of a component and remove descendants before parents; each removed stone still has its adjacent parent, so all but the root can be removed legally. Stone adjacency is exactly passage through a shared coordinate label, and every used-label component contains a stone. Thus label components and stone components correspond, and summing one mandatory survivor per component gives the maximum removals.
solution_outline.complexity: Expected `O(n α(n))` time with hashing and a balanced, path-compressed disjoint-set structure; `O(n)` auxiliary space for at most two labels per stone.
solution_outline.pitfall: A row number and an equal column number are different labels; merging their namespaces invents connections between unrelated stones.

common_wrong_turns: A row number and an equal column number are different labels; merging their namespaces invents connections between unrelated stones.
source_fidelity_notes: Retained sequential legality, shared-coordinate relationships, distinct occupied points, and all bounds; omitted removal traces.
